source_caption:
He got better with every word. 🥃

Matt Damon was cast as Rannulph Junuh in The Legend of Bagger Vance (2000) after Robert Redford sought a younger actor than himself for the role and Brad Pitt passed, with Damon eager to work under Redford's direction. Damon’s performance as the disillusioned, traumatized war veteran searching for his "authentic swing" was central to this tale of redemption. 

Based on the novel by Steven Pressfield, the film draws deep inspiration from the Bhagavad Gita, focusing on the spiritual and psychological recovery of a man who has lost his way.

source_details.title: The Legend of Bagger Vance
source_details.synopsis: The Legend of Bagger Vance is a 2000 American sports fantasy drama film directed by Robert Redford, and starring Will Smith, Matt Damon, and Charlize Theron. The screenplay by Jeremy Leven is based on Steven Pressfield's 1995 book The Legend of Bagger Vance: A Novel of Golf and the Game of Life. The film is set in 1931 Georgia. It was the final film starring Jack Lemmon and Lane Smith. The Legend of Bagger Vance was produced by Allied Filmmakers and Wildwood Enterprises and released on November 3, 2000, by DreamWorks Pictures in the United States and Canada and by 20th Century Fox internationally.
